Computational Details:
All spin-polarized density functional theory (DFT) calculations were performed using the Quickstep module of the CP2K package within the Gaussian and plane waves (GPW) framework. The Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functional combined with Grimme's DFT-D3(BJ) dispersion correction was employed to describe exchange-correlation and van der Waals interactions. Core electrons were represented by Goedecker-Teter-Hutter (GTH) pseudopotentials explicitly matched to double-zeta valence polarized molecularly optimized basis sets: GTH-PBE-q11 / DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH-q11 for Cu, GTH-PBE-q14 / DZVP-MOLOPT-SR-GTH-q14 for Sn (explicitly treating the 4d semicore electrons), and GTH-PBE-q4/q6/q1 / DZVP-MOLOPT-GTH for C, O, and H, with a plane-wave density cutoff of 500 Ry and a relative cutoff of 60 Ry. To construct computationally tractable, charge-neutral local models representative of the tannic-acid-derived metal-coordination environment, four-gallate dinuclear coordination motifs chelating two Cu2+ centers (Cu-20: [Cu2(C7H5O5)4]0 + Cu13, 70 support atoms + 13 cluster atoms = 83 atoms, 417 valence electrons, net charge 0) and a Sn(IV)-containing oxygen-coordinated polyphenol environment bridging Cu2+ with Sn4+ accompanied by charge-compensating ligand deprotonation and a coordinating H2O molecule (SnCu-20: [CuSn(C7H5O5)2(C7H4O5)2(H2O)]0 + Cu13, 71 support atoms + 13 cluster atoms = 84 atoms, 426 valence electrons, net charge 0, without Cu-Sn alloying or discrete oxide phases) were built to match the local Cu-O bond distances derived from EXAFS fitting. An identical icosahedral Cu13 cluster was anchored on both supports; theoretical Cu-Cu interatomic distances were compared with EXAFS bond-length trends while noting that ensemble-averaged experimental coordination numbers are not directly equivalent to those of an isolated finite cluster. All models were centered in a 30.0 × 30.0 × 30.0 Å3 cubic cell with non-periodic boundary conditions enforced in both the cell and Poisson solver (PERIODIC NONE, Martyna-Tuckerman solver), verified against a 34.0 × 34.0 × 34.0 Å3 cell to ensure full electron-density tail decay.

Initial cluster-support orientations and *HCCO adsorption configurations (including representative top and cluster-edge sites) were pre-relaxed using the Atomic Simulation Environment (ASE) coupled with the MACE-MP-0 machine learning interatomic potential (fmax < 0.05 eV/Å) solely as a structure generator without relying on MACE energy rankings to eliminate distinct coordination topologies or adsorption sites. For each system, 3-4 chemically distinct candidate configurations were subsequently optimized at the DFT level using matrix diagonalization with Fermi-Dirac smearing (300 K) and Broyden density mixing (force threshold < 0.01 eV/Å, SCF threshold 10^-6 Ha) after verifying the spin multiplicities of isolated fragments and odd/even-electron full complexes (doublet/quartet for Cu-20 and singlet/triplet for SnCu-20). Thermodynamic reaction free energies (ΔG = ΔE_DFT + ΔE_ZPE - TΔS) for the competing single-(H+/e-) protonation branches (*HCCO + H+ + e- → *H2CCO vs. *HCCO + H+ + e- → *HCCOH) were evaluated via the computational hydrogen electrode (CHE) model at U = 0 V vs. RHE and T = 298.15 K, noting that electrode potential and pH terms cancel identically in the relative selectivity difference (ΔΔG = ΔG_*H2CCO - ΔG_*HCCOH). Zero-point energy and entropic corrections for adsorbed intermediates were obtained via partial Hessian vibrational analyses implemented through ASE finite displacements (±0.01 Å) interfaced with CP2K static force evaluations (SCF threshold tightened to 10^-8 Ha, keeping the 70/71-atom support and Cu13 cluster fixed under the local vibrational approximation). Ketene desorption (*H2CCO → H2CCO(g) + *) was evaluated separately while neglecting vibrational free-energy changes of the bare catalyst framework. Electrostatic implicit solvation sensitivity checks (SCCS with ε = 78.4) and basis-set sensitivity checks (TZV2P-MOLOPT-GTH) were carried out on key states. Charge density differences (Δρ = ρ_total - ρ_Cu13 - ρ_support, evaluated on identical grids, cells, and basis sets with neutral fragment states), Bader charges, and vacuum-aligned projected density of states (PDOS) were processed using Multiwfn 3.8.

To investigate the electronic and thermodynamic effects of the Sn(IV)-containing oxygen-coordinated polyphenol environment on CO reduction selectivity, spin-polarized DFT calculations were performed on charge-neutral Cu-20 (70-atom four-gallate dinuclear support + Cu13 = 83 atoms) and SnCu-20 (71-atom Sn(IV)-modified support + Cu13 = 84 atoms) local models featuring identical Cu13 clusters (Figure X). In the optimized ground-state structures, the average support Cu-O bond lengths in Cu-20 and SnCu-20 are [X.XX] Å and [X.XX] Å, respectively, while the average Cu-Cu interatomic distance within the Cu13 cluster shifts from [X.XX] Å in Cu-20 to [X.XX] Å in SnCu-20, consistent with the local bond-length trends observed by EXAFS.

Charge density difference (Δρ) maps and Bader charge analyses evaluated under identical grid and basis-set conditions quantify the interfacial charge redistribution induced by the Sn(IV)-containing oxygen-coordinated polyphenol motif (Figure X). Specifically, the net Bader charge on the Cu13 cluster changes from [q_Cu20] |e| in Cu-20 to [q_SnCu20] |e| in SnCu-20, indicating that the Sn(IV)-modified polyphenol support renders the supported Cu13 cluster slightly more [electron-rich / electron-deficient / polarized] by [|Δq|] |e|. At the local adsorption site, the Bader charge of the coordinating Cu atoms shifts from [q_site1] |e| to [q_site2] |e|. Vacuum-aligned projected density of states (PDOS) analysis of the active Cu 3d states further shows that the auxiliary d-band center (εd) [upshifts / downshifts / remains nearly unchanged] from [εd_1] eV in Cu-20 to [εd_2] eV in SnCu-20 (Figure X), modulating the orbital interaction with adsorbed *HCCO.

We next compared the thermodynamic reaction free energies (ΔG) of the two competing adsorbed-state protonation branches starting from *HCCO at the representative [top / edge] active site under the CHE framework: terminal-carbon protonation toward adsorbed ketene (*HCCO + H+ + e- → *H2CCO) versus oxygen protonation toward *HCCOH (*HCCO + H+ + e- → *HCCOH). Upon incorporating the Sn(IV)-containing coordination motif, the C-C and C-O bond lengths of adsorbed *HCCO change from [d_CC1] Å and [d_CO1] Å (Cu-20) to [d_CC2] Å and [d_CO2] Å (SnCu-20), respectively. Thermodynamically, ΔG for *H2CCO formation [decreases / increases] from [ΔG1_Cu] eV on Cu-20 to [ΔG1_SnCu] eV on SnCu-20, whereas ΔG for *HCCOH formation [increases / decreases] from [ΔG2_Cu] eV to [ΔG2_SnCu] eV. Consequently, the selectivity-determining free energy difference between the two adsorbed branches (ΔΔG = ΔG_*H2CCO - ΔG_*HCCOH) shifts from [ΔΔG_Cu] eV on Cu-20 to [ΔΔG_SnCu] eV on SnCu-20, [indicating a favorable thermodynamic shift toward the *H2CCO branch at the sampled active site / reflecting competitive energetics between the two branches].
